subject: Finalizing OKR playbook + QBR materials — need exec endorsement
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Finalizing OKR playbook + QBR materials — need exec endorsement

Team — attaching the v2 playbook and the draft QBR slides. Goal is to lock the public-facing OKRs and the governance/approval flow by end of week so we can finalize slides for the board QBR on Oct 12. High-level asks: 

1) Read the attached OKR_Playbook_v2.docx and flag any scope or owner disagreements.
2) Confirm the proposed success criteria for each objective (in the doc).
3) Sign off (reply-all) or propose edits by EOD Thursday (Oct 6).

Quick summary of the proposed objectives (pulled from the doc):
- Objective A: Developer-first inference experience — increase host adoption and reduce median latency by 15%.
- Objective B: Production economics — reduce per-token cost by 12% through batching + caching + quantization profiles.
- Objective C: Reliability & SLA — achieve 99.95% availability for Redwood Dedicated customers.
- Objective D: Launch readiness — QBR-ready metrics, customer stories, and runbook updates.

Notes: I left tentative owners in the doc; if you want to swap owners, call it out explicitly. I also included a proposed governance flow (canary, A/B, rollback policy) and a short rollout-matrix.csv stub for ops.

Attachments: OKR_Playbook_v2.docx, QBR_Slides_Draft.pptx, rollout-matrix.csv

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | VP, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference
---
Onward: please keep replies concise so we can track signoffs.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finalizing OKR playbook + QBR materials — need exec endorsement

Marissa — thanks for pulling this together, strong draft. A couple of quick edits inline: 

- Objective A: can we explicitly add a latency SLO target for 95th percentile request latency for hosted API (keeping median as-is)? Suggest 95th <= 250ms for common models.
- Objective C: SLA is good, but I want an explicit incident budget and postmortem cadence called out in the governance section.

I've left comments in the Drive doc (linked). Otherwise I am OK with the owners you proposed.

If product-ops (Jonas) can map the rollout steps to the canary timeline, I think board slide will look clean.

Laura

Thanks all — good convergence. Summary / decisions to record here (final):

1) Objective names: adopt Grace's rename — 'Deployment Reliability & Cost Efficiency' for Obj B.
2) Latency SLO: add 95th <= 250ms for hosted API (Laura) — included in playbook.
3) Targets: we'll publish 'committed' vs 'stretch' columns (Vivek provided baselines and two stretch levels).
4) Governance: Jonas to own canary timeline and runbook; postmortem cadence and incident budget added.
5) Owners: owners in doc are final unless you tell me otherwise by EOD Oct 7.

Next steps (action items):
- Jonas: drop runbook link into the Drive doc by Oct 7.
- Grace: coordinate customer story blurbs by Oct 8.
- Vivek: loop Finance for revenue-impact validation by Oct 9.
- Laura: final review of SLA language by Oct 7.
- Marissa: collect signoffs and initiate DocuSign endorsement after Oct 9 if no objections.

I've uploaded okrs_targets.xlsx as an attachment and published the Drive links (see metadata). I'll start the DocuSign packet next week and share the link for signatures. If there are no further comments, consider this the formal endorsement thread.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | VP, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference
